A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DynaMix research, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.7. The material supports reliable matching and comparison without material evidence gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original dynamical-system simulations, empirical time-series evaluations, baseline comparisons, and ablation results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports additional evaluations of Chronos-2 and Panda.

M1.justification: The AL-RNN experts, CNN and attention gating, sparse teacher forcing, losses, and embedding extensions remain unchanged. Removing the optional zero-filling remark does not establish a changed training or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 34 training systems, 54 held-out three-dimensional systems, two-dimensional oscillators, Lorenz-96, and empirical datasets. The nonstationary Air Passengers example is also retained. New baselines are evaluated within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Figures 4, 5, and 23 and Tables 9–10 add Chronos-2 and Panda while removing Chronos-t5-tiny and Chronos-bolt-tiny. Figures 16–21 also add both new comparators. This substantially updates the central comparison, particularly by including the DS-pretrained Panda; empirical and custom-trained comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The retained training settings, context lengths, forecast horizons, metrics, preprocessing, and hardware controls are unchanged. The 10,000-step evaluation horizon emphasized in v3 was already documented in v2 Appendix A.1. The new comparators use the existing benchmark design.

E4.justification: Figures 16–21 extend existing qualitative case comparisons to Chronos-2 and Panda, adding evidence about their long-term failures; for example, both approach flat forecasts on the finance system. Component ablations, expert-count and teacher-forcing sensitivity studies, and embedding analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The captions of Figures 4 and 23 newly identify Wilcoxon signed-rank tests; v2 already displayed significance annotations without naming the test. Median/MAD and standard-deviation reporting practices remain unchanged, with no stated increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: Substantial comparative results are added for Chronos-2 and Panda at both context lengths, including detailed scores, forecast traces, and efficiency measurements; tiny-variant results are removed. At context length 2000, Figure 4 newly reports temporal distances of 0.28 and 0.25 respectively, below the previous best comparator's 0.30. DynaMix remains at 0.16, and numerical scores for retained methods are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical constructions and derivations are retained, with no new proofs. Equation 3 corrects the attention-vector dimension from T to TC, consistent with its existing formula. Added long-horizon guidance explains metric applicability without changing the underlying mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions retain the same claims about zero-shot DSR, long-term statistics, efficiency, and empirical generalization. Naming Panda in the conclusion and adding 'No other model tested achieved this' reiterate the existing comparative claim.

C2.justification: v3 adds the qualification that Panda's pretraining included variations of the test systems, favoring that comparator. Appendix A.1 more explicitly discusses long-horizon requirements for the reconstruction metrics and Lyapunov estimation. The main limitations concerning nonstationarity, temporal scales, and embeddings remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 newly documents Panda's pretraining on 20,000 combined dynamical systems and provides its evaluation-implementation pointer. DynaMix's implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware information, and Julia/Python code-access disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Chronos-2, Panda, and Wolf et al. on Lyapunov estimation, while retaining the previous references under revised numbering. Positioning expands locally to address Panda as a pretrained DS forecasting comparator.

P1.justification: There are localized explanatory additions, minor wording and notation corrections, and removal of the optional zero-filling aside. The narrative, section order, and appendix organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Comparison charts and table column groups are updated for the revised baselines. Figures 16–21 expand from six to eight forecast panels with revised legends, and Figure 7 gains panel labels. These are localized display changes within the retained document layout.

improvement.justification: Testing Chronos-2 and the DS-focused Panda strengthens support for the central comparison, while naming the statistical tests and clarifying long-horizon evaluation improve transparency. Two previously reported tiny-variant comparisons are lost, but the added comparator diversity provides a modest net benefit. The method, dataset coverage, and retained scores remain unchanged.
